task.name: run_sprint holds the sprint's execution state in a stack frame no other code can name, so every extraction from the module becomes a parameter-threading exercise
task.story_text:
## Why

ADR-0008 froze module size with a ratchet and recorded that bringing the frozen modules back under
the limit is a separate, deliberately sequenced effort. It also recorded why that effort cannot
start by splitting files, and this issue is the first unit it names.

`sprint/runner.py` is not 6,953 lines of evenly distributed code. It is a ~3,200-line module with
one function attached to the end:

| | |
|---|---|
| `run_sprint` | 3,754 lines — 54% of the file |
| other 67 top-level functions | median 30 lines |
| `run_sprint` parameters | 16 |
| functions nested inside `run_sprint` | 33, totalling 984 lines |
| distinct locals in `run_sprint` | 438 |
| locals captured by those nested closures | 117 |
| `nonlocal` names written by closures | `accumulated_cost`, `stopped_reason`, `ci_halt_slug` |

The nested functions are why nothing has been extracted. They are closures over the enclosing frame,
and three of them mutate it. They are nested because they capture state, not because anyone preferred
them there. `run_sprint` is already an object — 438 fields and 33 methods, none of which have names
anything can import.

Moving any one of them out today means threading five to fifteen parameters to the new home, which is
how the 16-parameter signature arose in the first place. The module-level helpers that look
extractable are the shallow copies; the behaviour lives in the closures.

This is upstream of throughput, not tidiness. Half of all stories landed since 2026-07-15 touch one
of the four oversized modules, and the scheduler serializes work on shared file claims, so these
modules convert independent parallel work into sequential work.

## Example

Today, the sprint's execution state exists only as a stack frame. Nothing can name it, construct it,
or assert against it, and three closures write to it through `nonlocal`:

```
run_sprint(...16 params...)
├─ 438 locals            # the real state; no name, no type, not importable
├─ _attempt_integration           ─┐
├─ _persist_current_story_result   │ 33 closures over 117 of those locals
├─ _record_dropped_story_audit     │ 3 of them write back via nonlocal:
├─ _resolve_queued_pr              │   accumulated_cost, stopped_reason, ci_halt_slug
└─ _service_plan_gates            ─┘
```

Wanted: that state is a named thing with an owner, so an extraction is a move rather than a
parameter-threading exercise. Two questions the `nonlocal` writes currently leave unanswered and
this issue has to settle: what accumulates cost, and what decides a sprint has stopped.

A worked case for the ownership question — today a closure both computes a story's cost and writes
it into the enclosing frame, so there is no single place that can answer "what has this sprint spent
and who last changed that figure." After this lands there is one.

## Acceptance criteria

- The state `run_sprint` currently holds in its frame is reachable by name from outside the function,
  so a caller can construct it and a test can assert against it without invoking a sprint.
- Cost accumulation has exactly one owner, which returns the accumulated figure and is the only thing
  that writes it, so no caller can advance the total by assigning to a shared variable.
- The sprint stop condition has exactly one owner on the same terms, which records both the reason a
  sprint stopped and any halt slug accompanying it.
- Where a value is read but never written by the nested functions, it stays read-only from them, so
  the split between what the sprint mutates and what it merely consults is expressed rather than
  implied.
- Sprint behaviour is unchanged: for the same inputs, the same stories run, in the same batches, with
  the same outcomes, costs and recorded audit fields as before the change. Any difference is a defect
  in this change rather than an accepted consequence of it.
- Whatever is not moved in this unit is left in a state where moving it later does not require
  re-deciding ownership, so subsequent extractions are downstream of this decision rather than
  reopening it.

## Out of scope

Splitting `sprint/runner.py` into multiple modules, and reducing any module below `max_module_lines`.
ADR-0008 records both as later units that are cheap only once this one has landed. The line count may
not fall as a result of this issue, and that is expected.

handoff.summary: Introduced four importable types in src/theforge/sprint/runner.py — SprintCostLedger (with SprintCostSnapshot), SprintStopCondition (with SprintStop), frozen SprintRunContext, and SprintExecutionState — and rewired run_sprint and its 30+ nested closures onto them. The context and state are constructed once, immediately after sprint_id resolution and after config/resolved settle; below that line the closures read _ctx and write _sprint_state. All three nonlocal writes (accumulated_cost, stopped_reason, ci_halt_slug) and the ad hoc cost_lock are removed: cost advances only through the ledger, whose record_story_cost pairs a story's cost with its unmeasured flag atomically, and whose snapshot() replaces the three lock blocks with one consistent read; stopping goes only through the stop condition, which records reason and halt slug together. The frame-local rewrite was done token-accurately (317 sites) so string literals and keyword-argument names were untouched, then ruff-formatted. Added 19 focused tests to tests/test_sprint_runner.py and recorded the ownership decision in src/theforge/sprint/CONVENTIONS.md so later extractions do not reopen it.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Cost accumulation has exactly one owner, which returns the accumulated figure and is the only thing that writes it, so no caller can advance the total by assigning to a shared variable.
acceptance_criteria.notes: SprintCostLedger owns accumulated, prior, unmeasured sources and the current-generation subset behind a lock; add() returns the new figure; accumulated/spent are read-only properties (assignment raises AttributeError, covered by test). test_only_the_ledger_advances_the_total reproduces the old nonlocal pattern (read out, reassign) and shows it cannot reach the total. Every former write site now calls add / record_story_cost / set_prior / flag_unmeasured_here / note_carried_unmeasured.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The sprint stop condition has exactly one owner on the same terms, which records both the reason a sprint stopped and any halt slug accompanying it.
acceptance_criteria.notes: SprintStopCondition holds a single frozen SprintStop(reason, halt_slug). reason/halt_slug are read-only properties. Two write methods preserve the two policies that existed in the original code: stop() unconditional (the CI-halt site, which previously assigned both variables unconditionally) and stop_if_unset() first-writer-wins (budget and auth-circuit sites, which were guarded by `if stopped_reason is None`). stop_if_unset returns whether it won, so the budget site's one-shot operator notification hangs off the same decision instead of re-deriving it.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Where a value is read but never written by the nested functions, it stays read-only from them, so the split between what the sprint mutates and what it merely consults is expressed rather than implied.
acceptance_criteria.notes: SprintRunContext is a frozen dataclass carrying config, resolved, sprint_id, run_id, auto_merge, interactive, notify, resume, reexec, no_pull, force, state_update_fn, dropped_slugs, skipped_issues, entry_intake_outcomes and the two live-slug sets (as frozensets). Rebinding any field raises FrozenInstanceError (tested). The context is constructed after the points where config and resolved are legitimately rebound during resolution (config replace, manifest resolve), so the prologue above that line still uses the plain names; everything from that line down — including all nested functions — reads _ctx. SprintCostSnapshot and SprintStop are frozen too, so a consulted read of cost or stop state cannot be written through.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Sprint behaviour is unchanged: for the same inputs, the same stories run, in the same batches, with the same outcomes, costs and recorded audit fields as before the change.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Full suite: 8217 passed, 38 skipped, 17 failed. The 17 failures are pre-existing sandbox permission errors in tests/test_cut_rc_isolation.py and tests/test_sprint_lock.py (mktemp and multiprocessing semaphores returning 'Operation not permitted'); verified they fail identically on HEAD before this change, and they are unrelated to runner.py. Existing run_sprint coverage (test_sprint_parallel, test_sprint_lifecycle, test_unmeasured_cost_reporting, test_coord_landing_precondition, test_sprint_terminal_lifecycle, test_sprint_surface_consistency and others) passes unchanged. Two locking details are now stricter but cannot change a single-threaded result: _story_allocation_entry's sprint_cost_measured flag and the dispatch budget check's unmeasured partition now come from the same snapshot as the total rather than being re-read outside the lock.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Whatever is not moved in this unit is left in a state where moving it later does not require re-deciding ownership.
acceptance_criteria.notes: src/theforge/sprint/CONVENTIONS.md now records the rule: sprint-wide state goes on SprintExecutionState (mutable) or SprintRunContext (consulted), never back into the frame or a nonlocal; cost and stop keep their single owners; and an extraction takes the context/state rather than a fresh set of threaded parameters. Locals still in the frame that a later unit will move (worker_phases and its phase_lock, story_deadlines, preflight_states, dag/batch bookkeeping) fall on one side of that line without further debate.

story_deviations: SprintExecutionState carries the sprint-wide outcome and accounting collections (cost, stop, story state, merged_slugs, results, story_times, live_telemetry_snapshots, batch_assignments, batch_number) rather than all 438 frame locals. Moving every local in one commit would be a mechanical change too large to review against a behavioural-parity bar; the ownership rule that decides where each remaining local goes is recorded in CONVENTIONS.md, which is what AC6 asks for.

runner.py grew by roughly 280 lines (the new types are in-file, per the plan's Step 1 and the out-of-scope note). check_net_new_violations excludes MODULE_LINES_RULE, so this shows up in the advisory report only.
deferred_items: worker_phases / phase_lock and the per-story scheduling dictionaries (story_deadlines, preflight_states, stop_events) remain frame locals; they are display and scheduler-local state whose move belongs with the extraction that takes the scheduler loop out.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

plan_structured.approach: Introduce a named, importable sprint execution state boundary inside the sprint runner, with separate single-owner components for mutable cost and stop state and read-only context for consulted values. Rewire run_sprint and its nested closures to use that boundary without changing scheduling, batching, audit, or outcome behavior.

steps.description: Define the sprint execution state ownership model
steps.details: Add top-level importable types in runner.py for the state currently trapped in run_sprint's frame: a mutable sprint execution state object, a single cost accumulator owner, a single stop-condition owner, and a read-only context for values closures only consult. Keep these types local to the runner module for this unit rather than splitting files.

steps.description: Route run_sprint through the named state object
steps.details: Construct the named execution state at the start of run_sprint and migrate frame locals into either mutable state ownership or read-only context according to how the nested closures use them. Preserve the existing public run_sprint call contract and sprint orchestration flow.

steps.description: Replace nonlocal writes with state-owner operations
steps.details: Remove the nonlocal mutations for accumulated_cost, stopped_reason, and ci_halt_slug. Make cost changes go only through the cost owner, and make sprint stopping go only through the stop-condition owner that records both reason and halt slug.

steps.description: Keep read-only closure inputs visibly read-only
steps.details: For captured values that nested functions read but never write, access them through the read-only context rather than mutable execution state. Leave later extraction candidates with stable ownership decisions instead of ad hoc parameter threading.

steps.description: Cover constructability, ownership, and behavioral parity
steps.details: Add or update focused sprint runner tests proving the new state types can be constructed and asserted against without invoking a sprint, cost cannot be advanced by shared-variable assignment, stop state records reason and halt slug through one owner, and representative sprint execution/audit behavior remains unchanged.

criteria_mapping.criterion: The state run_sprint currently holds in its frame is reachable by name from outside the function, so a caller can construct it and a test can assert against it without invoking a sprint.
Cost accumulation has exactly one owner, which returns the accumulated figure and is the only thing that writes it, so no caller can advance the total by assigning to a shared variable.
The sprint stop condition has exactly one owner on the same terms, which records both the reason a sprint stopped and any halt slug accompanying it.

Where a value is read but never written by the nested functions, it stays read-only from them, so the split between what the sprint mutates and what it merely consults is expressed rather than implied.

Sprint behaviour is unchanged: for the same inputs, the same stories run, in the same batches, with the same outcomes, costs and recorded audit fields as before the change. Any difference is a defect in this change rather than an accepted consequence of it.
Whatever is not moved in this unit is left in a state where moving it later does not require re-deciding ownership, so subsequent extractions are downstream of this decision rather than reopening it.
